title: A cubic permanent–determinant lower bound
manuscript_title: A cubic lower bound for border determinantal complexity of the permanent

base_library_L: Mathlib d13f23b + references.bib of the manuscript (30 entries, incl. SheshadriBorder2026 arXiv:2606.13628, KumarVolk2026 arXiv:2609.34462, CHT2023, FGvS1999, Galazka2017).

main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main} There exist absolute constants $c>0$ and $m_0$ such that, for every integer $m\ge m_0$, \[ \bdc(\per_m)\ge c m^3. \] One may take $c=1/(5\,529\,600e)$ and $m_0=1408$. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: Over C, if the m x m permanent is a coefficientwise limit of determinants of n x n matrices of affine-linear forms (n fixed along the sequence, coefficients unbounded), then n >= m^3/(5,529,600 e) for all m >= 1408. Exact determinantal complexity inherits the bound (Cor 9.1), and so do vertex and edge counts of affine ABPs, including fixed-budget limits (Cor 9.2).

constructive_core.latex: Prop smooth-projection: for k>=128, q=floor((k-1)/3), r=k-2q, d=floor(k^2/100) there is a nonzero form G of degree r in d variables with smooth projective zero set and, for every m>=11k-2q, an affine map Phi_m with G = per_m o Phi_m; r-1>=k/4, d-1>=k^2/200.
constructive_core.paraphrase: A linear-size permanent has an affine projection that is a smooth hypersurface of linear degree in quadratically many variables. This is then fed into the smooth-form bound bdc(G) >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e) (Thm 2.3).

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: Cor exact-complexity: dc(per_m) >= m^3/(5,529,600e) for m>=1408.
Cor ABP: affine-linear ABPs for per_m need Omega(m^3) vertices and Omega(m^3) edges, also in fixed-budget border limits (via ABP -> determinant of size N+1).

Cor smooth-initial-form: if the lowest homogeneous term of g(a+x) has degree r>=2 and is smooth in P^{d-1}, then bdc(g), dc(g) >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e). With Thm 2.3 this gives e.g. bdc(sum_i x_i^n) >= (n-1)^2/(4e), the bound claimed by the LLM-assisted Sheshadri preprint.
Thm smooth-border (supporting): smooth nonzero form of degree r>=2 in d>=2 variables has bdc >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e).

A.label: A5

secondary.explicit_rate_detail: c = 1/(5,529,600 e), m0 = 1408; Thm smooth-border also explicit (r-1)(d-1)/(4e).

evidence.quote: There exist absolute constants $c>0$ and $m_0$ such that, for every integer $m\ge m_0$, $\bdc(\per_m)\ge c m^3$.

A.note: Innermost conclusion is 'no (border) determinantal representation of size < c m^3 exists' = impossibility (A5) with explicit rate. A3 (quantitative) is the obvious alternative; the bound is not claimed sharp (Grenet's upper bound is 2^m - 1, introduction.tex:90-94).

B.label: B3

flags.full_only_with_prior_results_detail: Self-contained modulo cited AG facts: CHT2023 Severi dimension (dimension.tex:68-75, essential, not re-proved) and Stacks semicontinuity/constructibility. Lean replaces these by its own proofs.
flags.adds_corollaries_detail: Cubic ABP vertex/edge lower bounds for per_m (previous best quadratic, Kumar/CKSV for other polynomials); smooth-form bound gives bdc(sum x_i^n) >= (n-1)^2/(4e), i.e. a self-contained proof of the claim of the LLM-written Sheshadri preprint 2606.13628 that Kumar-Volk (2609.34462) could not verify.

B.secondary_label: B4 (raises the exponent of the Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre m^2/2 border bound and of Mignon-Ressayre's exact m^2/2 bound to 3)

evidence.quote: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} raises the lower-bound exponent from two to three in that same model. It remains a fixed polynomial bound. Whether the permanent has superpolynomial determinantal complexity ... remains open.

B.note: The posed problem (permanent vs determinant / Valiant's conjecture) is superpolynomial; this is partial progress (B3). Relative to the specific quadratic-bound literature it is B4. Recorded B3 primary because the family title frames it as a permanent-determinant result.

secondaries.label: C5

evidence.quote: Applying the arbitrary-characteristic Severi dimension theorem of Christ, He and Tyomkin ... bounds the locus of curves with this defect.

secondaries.note: Two genuine reductions: per_m -> smooth form G by a fixed affine projection (Cor selector-border), and a char-2 -> char-0 transfer of the gradient-locus bound (Lemma characteristic-transfer). CHT2023 Severi dimension is invoked without proof (essential in the paper; bypassed in Lean).

secondaries.label: C1

evidence.quote: two count gates and a cancellation gadget realize $G_D$, up to a fixed nonzero scalar, as an affine restriction of a permanent of size $11k-2q$

secondaries.note: Explicit gadget construction (Prop selector). Not primary: it builds an auxiliary projection, not the witness of the headline (a universal lower bound).

secondaries.label: C3

evidence.quote: Specialization transfers the dimension bound to a nonempty open set of complex parameters ... a general linear section avoids that scheme

secondaries.note: Non-constructive existence of good parameters theta and of a smooth section H (dimension counts on Grassmannians/parameter spaces); the smooth form G is never written down.

computer_assisted_evidence.quote: To verify the six balanced cases, first $\per H=-2$.

C.computer_assisted_note: All verifications are by hand (3x3 gadget permanents, binomial estimates). Lean decide uses are Bool/literal side conditions only. The gadget weights could have come from a search, but nothing in the proof depends on one.
C.ih_note: No induction on statements. The Hilbert-scheme bound stratifies by length types (dimension.tex:298-309); the product count uses a homotopy (polar.tex:146-176). Neither is an induction hypothesis.
C.confidence: medium (C4 vs C5 primary is arguable: the cubic comes from one comparison of counts, but most of the paper is reduction + dimension theory)

D.label: D3
D.max_item: I06 coefficient polynomial G_D = [s^q t^q] per_k(X+sI+tD) used as a smooth-after-slicing permanent projection (N3, F1/F3), with I29/I32/I35 (char-2 spectral-curve bound on the gradient locus: grad G = 0 => delta(C_X) >= T => codim >= T-k; N3, F5) as co-candidate. The smooth-form bound I13/I48 is N2 (close variant of LLM-written Sheshadri 2606.13628).

evidence.quote: we seek an affine restriction of a permanent of size proportional to $k$ that has degree proportional to $k$ in quadratically many variables and has a smooth projective zero set.

caveats: Quick check found a model-produced architectural precedent NOT cited by the paper: OpenAI 'Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science' (Aug 1 2026), Chapter 5 / github openai/ten-proofs Permanent.lean defines minorSum t s d (sum of permanental minors), criticalLocus dimension and homogeneous linear slices with finite gradient zero sets, for an n^2 log log n circuit bound (described in Guo arXiv:2609.29568). The 'affine specialization of the permanent with small critical locus + generic slice' idea is therefore not new to 108; I06 may drop to N2.

The smooth-form half (Thm smooth-border) has the same constant 4e and the same kernel-lift + multihomogeneous Bezout architecture as Sheshadri 2606.13628 (acknowledgement: 'The author used the assistance of large language models in all stages of the effort.'). The paper cites it as the source of the kernel equations (polar.tex:9-13).
Cross-field imports (Severi dimension, conductor/delta, Hilbert schemes, polar degree, Bertini) are N0 transfer and never yield D3 on their own.
D.flag_detail: Cites and builds on SheshadriBorder2026 (LLM-assisted in all stages, per its acknowledgement) for the kernel-equation/Schur architecture of the smooth-form bound. Does not cite the earlier OpenAI Ten Advances permanent chapter, whose critical-locus/slice architecture it follows. Also cites KumarVolk2026 (dated 28 Sep 2026, i.e. after the manuscript's 24 Sep date).

proof_architecture.claim: Model: bdc monotone under fixed affine substitution; coefficientwise = orbit-closure model.
Selector: G_D = [s^q t^q] per_k(X+sI+tD) is (up to a0 != 0) an affine projection of per_m for m >= 11k-2q, any complex D.

Char 2: per = det, so a critical X of G_Dbar (distinct theta) gives a spectral curve C_X whose adjugate scheme has length >= T (catalecticant trick) and length Z <= delta(C_X) (conductor). Hence delta(C_X) >= T.

Count: curves with delta >= T have dim <= k(k+3)/2 - T (Severi, CHT2023); matrices over a fixed curve have dim <= k(k-1)/2 (row subscheme + Hilb^N bound). So codim of the gradient locus >= T - k ~ k^2/18.
Transfer to C for generic theta (proper family over Z[theta]); Euler identity identifies gradient locus with Sing; a generic d = k^2/100-dimensional linear section is smooth.

Smooth-form bound: a border limit of n x n affine determinants with a smooth degree-r form in d variables has r(r-1)^{d-2} simple polar points, which persist in one close determinant, lift uniquely and simply to the bilinear kernel system, and are bounded by the multihomogeneous Bezout number 2^{d-2} binom(2n-1, d-1). Hence n >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e).
Combine: bdc(per_m) >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e) >= k^3/(3200e) with k = floor(m/11); corollaries for dc, ABPs, initial forms.

lean_route_differences: Severi step (paper: CHT2023 cited, codim T) -> Lean: elementary char-2 Frobenius 'squareForm' analysis bounding delta by 5*dim(half-ideal quotient) + #ordinary singular points, then a transcendence-degree parameter count giving 18n + T <= 9(k+1)(k+2) (ConductorDimension.lean:290,430; Main.lean:131). Weaker by ~18x in T; not described in the paper or lean/docs/108.md.

Dimension notion: paper uses scheme dimension; Lean uses ringKrullDim of the quotient by the gradient ideal, bounded through transcendence degrees of field-valued points (DeterminantFields.krullDim_le_of_field_images).

Gradient-locus bound: paper dim <= k^2 + k - T; Lean ringKrullDim <= k^2 - T/18 (Main.lean:214-257). Section size: paper d = floor(k^2/100); Lean sectionSize = T/18 with (d-1) >= k^2/330 and r-1 >= 0.33k (Main.lean:259-311). The final constant 1/(5529600e) is the same because the paper's constant had slack.

Matrix fibre / Hilbert scheme: paper uses a Hilbert-scheme incidence; Lean uses trdeg bounds over quotient-field charts and canonical nilpotent forms (PunctualCharts, Nilpotents, QuotientFields). The paper's row-uniqueness lemma is formalized (RowIdeals.matrix_eq_of_rowIdeal_eq) but is not on the target's dependency path.

Char transfer and smooth slicing: paper uses proper-family semicontinuity (Stacks 0D4I) and a Grassmannian incidence; Lean uses Macaulay-matrix surjectivity certificates with algebraically independent slice coefficients (ConditionalBound, Transcendence, SmoothSlices).

Smooth-form bound: the Lean polar count goes through a homotopy/covering argument (RegularSections.proper_localHomeomorph_card) and Vandermonde product charts (ProjectiveCounts, LinearForms), as in the paper.

correctness_audit.verdict: Plausible and largely checked at sketch level, with strong formal support. Headline and smooth-initial-form statements have exact comparators, the library has no sorry/axioms, and Lean independently re-proves the steps that depend on cited heavy AG (Severi), so the Lean result does not rest on CHT2023. Lean was not run here. The claim would be a major advance (first super-quadratic border/exact dc bound for per; first cubic ABP bound for per), so an external referee check of the paper route is still warranted.
checked: Gadget arithmetic: per H = -2; deleting one interface row and column gives [[-1,1],[1,1]] with permanent 0; H33 = 1 with external product -2w. Size count k + 2(2k-q) + 6k = 11k-2q.
Count gate forces exactly q diagonal edges with multiplicity (h!)^2.
dF_X/dX_ij = u adj(M)_ji, so grad G_D = 0 iff [s^q t^q u^{r-1}] adj M = 0. The catalecticant step recovers every coefficient of a degree-q form since q <= c = r-1.

Dimension count: generic fibre dim k^2 - k(k+1)/2 = k(k-1)/2 = N, consistent with Prop matrix-fiber. Using the full linear-system Severi bound (k(k+3)/2 - T) instead of the fixed-fibre subspace costs only +k.
Polar count: (h+2n-1) equations on P^{h+1} x P^{n-1} x P^{n-1}; coefficient <= 2^h binom(2n-1,h+1); root extraction gives n >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e).

Sanity vs upper bounds: the det-analogue [s^q t^q] det(X+sI+tD) is congruent to G_D mod 2, so the same argument gives it dc >= c k^3; its trivial upper bound is about T*k ~ k^3/18 (interpolation over T determinants). No contradiction. Smooth Fermat forms: dc O(rd) vs bound (r-1)(d-1)/4e, consistent.
residual_concerns: CHT2023 Severi dimension in characteristic 2 for all integral curves (not only nodal) is cited precisely but not re-proved; the Lean route avoids it.
